detail.body:
## Summary

Replace separate forward and backward execution orders with one weakly held sequence of `ExecutionEvent(module, phase)` values and one cursor. Registration mode populates the sequence during construction; recorded mode populates it from execution. Both use the same traversal.

## Implementation

- Validate each observed module and phase against the event at the cursor, raising on divergence.
- Use argument-free `advance()`, which automatically wraps at the end of the sequence.
- Prefetch successive events using each event's phase and the existing prefetch budget. Forward/backward phase changes do not stop lookahead.
- Preserve every recorded occurrence, including repeated calls to the same module.
- Test registration-order divergence with a model that executes its two layers in the opposite order from registration.
- Use recording mode for the shared-MTP regression, whose shared block runs twice per forward pass; retain its five-step comparison with unsharded training.

The execution-order implementation follows #8721. This PR changes three production files and three test files. Complete schedule-window recording, PP/VPP and EP-overlap integration, and evaluation handling are covered separately in #8778.

## Validation

Rebased onto `main` at `bfab98f4a`, preserving the extracted MCore adapters and the updated communication-stream policies.

Exact commit `158b2b6ac3f426dce63e1d4ec4006b3418533869`: Docker validation on **two RTX A6000 GPUs passed 93 tests on each rank**, with five tests skipped because they require four ranks. Ran the complete execution-order, context, fully-shard, and pipeline-context test files. Coverage includes shared-MTP training, registration-order divergence, recorded replay, activation recomputation, and HSDP/HFSDP loss comparisons.

Black, isort, Pylint, Ruff, and `git diff --check` passed. The cached dev CI image uses NGC 26.08; the repository pins 26.09.

## Code provenance

Refactors this repository's FSDP implementation and tests, incorporating the simplification from #8721. Existing copyright and license notices are preserved. No code copied from other repositories.

```suggestion
ExecutionEvent = tuple[nn.Module, Phase]
```
I've been trying to avoid circular dependencies. So FsdpModule -> FsdpContext -> ExecutionOrder -> nn.Module is OK but FsdpModule -> FsdpContext -> ExecutionOrder -> FsdpModule is not. 

Nit: I'd also prefer NamedTuple so it's harder for the caller to make mistakes when we add more attributes to ExecutionEvent.

The `position` allows us to maintain an unshardable interval within the context.

This addresses the issue with the two cursors: the `unshard` cursor and the `prefetch` cursor. A single `FsdpModule.unshard` call may trigger prefetching for zero or more modules, but the unshard cursor advances only once per call.

My first instinct says it shouldn't because forward and backward can interleave in PP and VPP. @wujingyue Yes, I agree—we shouldn't impose phase boundaries on prefetching. If `execution_order` spans multiple microbatches, prefetching should be able to cross those boundaries as well. While comparing DSv4 Flash performance with ZeRO-3 (M-FSDP v2 + MXFP8) and ZeRO-1 (DistOpt + MXFP8), I found that the all-gather at the start of each microbatch and the reduce-scatter (RS) at the end account for a **10% gap in step time**. Prefetching the next microbatch's module weights could help narrow this gap by unblock next microbatch executing.
